transcript.text: Every time I put the oven on it runs for a few minutes and then the trip switch goes and half the house loses power. Reset it 3 times tonight. Hotpoint built-in, about 9 years old. What could cause this?

⚠ Stop using this appliance
Please don't keep resetting the trip. Leave the appliance unplugged and have it checked by a qualified electrician or appliance engineer before using it again. This is an electrical safety fault. The fact that the trip switch (RCD) goes off means there is a leakage of electricity to earth inside the oven—most commonly from a heating element whose insulation has broken down as it heats up. It could also be internal wiring or the terminal block where the mains cable connects. Because this involves live electrical components and potential fire risk, you must stop using the oven immediately. Do not reset the switch again to try and use it; repeated tripping can damage your home's wiring and poses a serious shock hazard. A qualified electrician or appliance engineer needs to isolate the supply and test the internal insulation resistance to find exactly which component is failing. Please arrange for a professional inspection before using the appliance again.

candidates: Heating element leaking to earth (RCD fault) (high)
Internal wiring or terminal block overheating/leaking (medium)

reading.symptom: runs for a few minutes and then the trip switch goes and half the house loses power

plan: They asked: "What could cause this?" - answer that first.

Safety: a supply trip hazard is active. The fixed safety warning is shown separately, do not repeat it. It must not be used again until a qualified engineer has checked it: say that plainly. You may explain the likely cause and suggest checks that are safe with it switched off and unplugged, but never say or imply that a check could make it safe to use, or that they might not need an engineer.
Checks they have done and what they found: reset trip switch - did it 3 times tonight.
Already given by the customer, never ask for it again: make Hotpoint.
The fault they reported is: "runs for a few minutes and then the trip switch goes and half the house loses power". Keep to it: never describe a symptom, result or state they have not told you.
They asked about something unsafe (repeated reset): do not explain how to do it; the fixed safety wording is shown separately. Offer the safe alternative.

Stage 1 (broad help): say what could cause this, most likely first, as possibilities rather than certainties, including simple causes (settings, loading, detergent, installation, or normal behaviour) where they fit. Then give the safe checks that best tell those causes apart (most useful and simplest first, usually two to four), each with why it helps and what each result would mean; or, if one question would settle it sooner, ask that. Do not ask for the model number in this reply. Do not tell them to buy, order or replace a part yet.

facts.value: reset trip switch: did it 3 times tonight
